t.w2_body: The Maasai named the Mara for how it looks from a distance: open plains spotted with acacia trees, bushes and the shadows of passing clouds. On your first game drive, you’ll see it too.

t.story_title: Two Maasai sisters, one vision: the story of Oloning’o
t.story_1: Three decades ago, Siimoi left her Maasai homeland and made Germany her home. A trained nurse by profession, she built a life dedicated to caring for others, carrying with her the values, traditions and rich cultural heritage of the Maasai people to whom she belongs.
t.story_2: Born Maasai and raised within the traditions of her people, Siimoi has always carried a deep connection to her roots, even while building her life abroad. Over the years, people often asked her about her homeland, its culture, traditions and the extraordinary landscapes of Kenya. Yet tourism was never part of her professional journey. Nursing was her calling, and safari was a world she had not imagined herself becoming part of.
t.story_3: That began to change when an opportunity arose through her younger sister, Cecilia.
t.story_4: A proud Maasai woman herself, Cecilia has dedicated 25 years to the hospitality industry, building extensive experience in guest service, camp operations and the art of creating memorable safari experiences. Inspired by her love for her homeland and her desire to make a lasting difference, she established Oloning’o Mara Camp, a women-led company in the heart of the Maasai Mara.
t.story_5: Cecilia’s vision was about more than creating a safari destination. She wanted to create employment opportunities for women in her community, support their economic independence, empower future generations and contribute to the long-term sustainability of the land and the people who call it home.
t.story_6: Through Cecilia’s vision, Siimoi began to see a new opportunity to connect her life in Germany with the heritage she had carried across continents. The questions people had always asked her about Maasai culture and Kenya could become a meaningful way to introduce travellers to her homeland while supporting the community they both love.
t.story_meet: This is where their journeys meet.
t.story_7: Oloning’o Travel in Germany and Oloning’o Mara Camp in Kenya represent the coming together of two Maasai sisters, two countries and one shared heritage.
t.brings_s: Her experience of living in Germany, her nursing background and her ability to connect with people interested in discovering Africa.
t.brings_c: 25 years of hospitality experience, her knowledge of the Maasai Mara and her commitment to building a business that creates opportunities for women and supports sustainable tourism.
t.story_8: Together, the sisters aspire to build a bridge between Germany and Kenya, inviting travellers to experience the beauty, culture and spirit of the Maasai Mara while contributing to a more inclusive and sustainable future for their community.
t.story_9: For Siimoi and Cecilia, Oloning’o is more than a name. It represents their identity, their connection to their Maasai heritage and their shared determination to create opportunities for the generations that follow them.
t.story_closing: Two Maasai sisters. Two countries. One heritage. One shared vision for a sustainable future.
